summary: Round-7 repairs the round-6 prose defects correctly and the MAX_HEAL_PASSES cap does achieve its stated purpose, but the cap's check is placed one pass too early and one prose figure is still wrong; both are this round's own defects, so the candidate FAILs. F-1: the cap IS load-bearing — with a pathological writer the real candidate stops at 8 passes in 1ms while my cap-disabled mutant of the same source ran 201 passes and was stopped only by my harness gate; the termination goal is met. But `if (passes >= MAX_HEAL_PASSES)` at queueStore.ts:939 sits BEFORE the zero-candidate rescan at :948-953, so the loop exits at the end of pass 8 without rescanning, one full pass early. With a bounded writer that re-arms a stale `true` 9 times, the real candidate ends with the marker still `true` (node stuck '排队中', button disabled) while the cap-disabled mutant heals it on pass 10; at 12 re-arms, same divergence (8 vs 13). The same placement also produces a false-alarm warning at 7 re-arms: the marker IS healed but console.warn still claims '仍有陈旧 queued 标记未复核'. Moving the cap block below the :953 zero-candidate check removes both effects at zero cost. F-2..F-5 are genuinely closed: the `true|idle` marker set is real (written at useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:138-142 with status 'idle') and honestly marked non-exhaustive; the normal-path figures are TRUE by instrumentation not trust (passes=1, predicate=1, self-inflicted identity change=1, break-at-healPending 0 times, exit at zero-candidate rescan 1 time, re-entry 1, healPending set 1 — every number in the :925-933/:950-952 comment is exact); the hook's write-site claim is exactly 3 (imageGenerationExecution.ts:213, :227, :267); the 0-back-edge half of the dependency claim is confirmed (flowStore/canvasStore do not import queueStore) but the count is wrong — the real static import graph gives 22 in-repo files + 7 bare externals, and 22 under every methodology I tried, so '21' is unsubstantiated. F-R5-1, F-R5-2, F-R4-1 and F-R3-2 all remain closed: probes show a rejected click toasts with zero node-data writes and zero job growth, a stale marker introduced during the heal is still corrected in every carrier while legitimate markers survive, undo/cancel/Ctrl+Z and the restart path both leave the marker false in both carriers, and a falsy marker still costs zero writes/zero identity change/zero subscriber hits. Gate honesty confirmed: queue-regression 6/6 PASS exit 0 and tsc exit 0, but the gate has 0 matches for undo|redo|saveToHistory, so it is BLIND to the round-4/5/6 findings and its green is not evidence for them. The worker's two counter-claims are corroborated with corrections: r6-fix2-defer ⑥'s failure IS a stale expectation (8 is the cap signature, companion bound PASSes), and the r6-fix1-feedback / r6-window-hunt failures ARE fixture bugs (an n=4 accepted click enqueues +4, not +1; and a sleep(120) that lands past the second job's start). The worker's 'byte-identical A/B' is not reproduced — my wrapper attempt failed and I stopped rather than burn budget — but the two fixture bugs behind it are independently confirmed. The probes-load-two-queueStore-instances hazard is real and did contaminate my first mutant run until I force-resolved a single instance.
findings: queueStore.ts:937-953 (defect introduced THIS round) — the MAX_HEAL_PASSES check at :939 is placed before the zero-candidate rescan at :948-953, so the loop exits at the END of pass 8 without rescanning: one full pass earlier than the pre-round-7 code. Trigger: any bounded writer that re-arms a stale queued:true N>=9 times. Impact (measured, deterministic 3/3, single queueStore instance forced): with N=9 the real candidate ends with passes=8 and the marker still `true` — the node shows '排队中' with the generate button disabled, i.e. the REQ-001 symptom class the heal exists to prevent — whereas a mutant of the SAME source with MAX_HEAL_PASSES=Infinity runs passes=10 and ends with the marker `false`, proving pass 9 would have cleared it; with N=12 the divergence is passes=8 marker true vs passes=13 marker false. Scope honestly: no in-repo writer re-arms (the in-repo writers are one-shot), so this is a demonstrated loss of safety margin versus round 6, not a reproduced in-app symptom. Same placement, second effect: with N=7 the marker IS healed (false) yet console.warn still fires with '仍有陈旧 queued 标记未复核', a false alarm. Suggestion: move the :938-947 cap block to AFTER the zero-candidate check at :953 (i.e. check the cap only once a further pass is actually known to be needed), which restores the round-6 outcome for every bounded writer and silences the false positive at no cost; if the ordering is deliberately kept, the warning text must stop asserting an unhealed candidate and the comment at :854-860 ('上限之上的代价是可能漏掉一次治疗') should state that the cost can also be paid one pass early.

queueStore.ts:824 (prose over-claim, same class that failed rounds 3, 4, 5 and 6) — the comment states the static import graph from queueStore contains '仓库内传递依赖 21 个文件 + 7 个外部裸模块'. My own traversal of the real import graph gives 22 in-repo files + 7 bare externals (@tauri-apps/api/core, @tauri-apps/plugin-store, @xyflow/react, lucide-react, uuid, zustand, zustand/middleware), and 22 under every methodology I tried: all static imports = 22; including re-exports = 45; excluding src/types/** entirely = 20. No natural method yields 21, so the corrected figure is itself an estimate rather than a count. Trigger: any reader who trusts the number. Impact: low (no behavior), but this is precisely the defect class that produced a finding in each of the last four rounds, and the comment presents the number as '实测'. The load-bearing half of the claim — 0 back-edges, no module-initialization cycle — is CONFIRMED: flowStore.ts and canvasStore.ts contain no queueStore import, and my traversal found 0 back-edges. Suggestion: drop the file count (it drifts with the code, as the comment itself concedes) and keep only the independently re-verified '0 back-edges' conclusion, or replace the number with the method used to produce it.

Non-blocking observation (not counted as a defect): console.warn at queueStore.ts:942 is consistent with this codebase's conventions — src/ contains 71 console.* sites and 14 in src/stores alone, including queueStore.ts:552 console.error and flowStore.ts's console.warn calls — so a dev-only guard is not required for consistency and the warn is appropriate. Its only issue is the wording/condition covered by finding 1.

review_checks.analysis: REQ-001 (a leftover queued job must not leave the node locked showing '排队中' with the button disabled after restart) and REQ-002 (repeated clicks on one node must not create concurrent jobs for the same node) were tested independently of the gate, which is blind here (0 matches for undo|redo|saveToHistory in scripts/queue-regression.mjs). REQ-002 holds and is not weakened: probe-r4-guard2 12/12 PASS including 'not global single-flight' and 'paused not consulted by the guard'; the guard is synchronous inside enqueue, scoped to same nodeId AND same (canvasId ?? null), counts only queued||running, never historical, never running-only; a rejected click still adds zero jobs (r6-window-hunt guardLeaks=0, r6-fix1-feedback jobs unchanged). REQ-001 holds on the real paths: probe-req001-coldstart '节点可用（REQ-001 已修复）'; probe-lock-via-ui '未形成永久锁'; probe-cancel-abort-lock '未形成永久锁'; probe-r4-undo-cancel → marker false after cancel, after Ctrl+Z, and in the persisted canvasStore copy; probe-r4-undo-restart restart phase → marker false in both carriers with 0 recoverable jobs. REQ-001 does NOT fully hold against the round-7 cap, however: my instrumented probe shows a bounded writer that re-arms a stale true 9 times leaves the marker `true` at exit (passes=8) where the cap-disabled mutant heals it (passes=10), i.e. the cap can leave a node in exactly the locked state REQ-001 exists to prevent. No in-repo writer re-arms, so the real-app requirement is met today; the failure is a self-inflicted regression in the safety margin of the mechanism itself, which is why this area is FAIL rather than PASS.

Standing properties and every previously-closed finding were re-tested against this candidate. Still closed: F-R3-2 (when the marker is already falsy there are zero writes, zero identity change, zero subscriber hits and zero canvas-store writes — the early return precedes the reentrancy flag and any write; probe-r3-finally-churn reports 0 App.tsx-shaped subscribe hits), F-R5-2 (a stale true introduced by a third-party subscriber DURING the heal is still corrected in both flowStore and the canvas copy, and a legitimate marker belonging to a queued job on another canvas is preserved — r6-fix2-defer ①/②/③ PASS; my probe C independently confirms correction and carrier coverage), F-R5-1 (in a real n=4/concurrency=1/unpaused batch each rejected click produces exactly one toast, writes no node data field, and adds no job, while an accepted click produces no toast — r6-window-hunt 4/4 feedback, dataWritesOnReject=0, guardLeaks=0; r6-fix1-feedback toast 0→1 on rejection, data unchanged, marker not written back to true), F-R4-1 (undo/redo resurrection retracted: probe-r4-undo-cancel '未复现' with snapshot containing queued:true then Ctrl+Z leaving the marker false in both carriers; probe-r4-undo-restart '未复现' with the persisted canvasStore copy also false). Batch/cross-canvas/unified-scope behavior intact: probe-batch-chain 15/15, probe-cross-canvas '两画布互不干扰', probe-reject-timeline and probe-reject-erases-marker both '未复现'. Typecheck exit 0. The regression FAIL is the round-7 cap itself: with N=9 and N=12 bounded re-arms the loop exits at 8 passes leaving the marker true where the cap-disabled mutant of the same source heals it at pass 10/13, and with N=7 it warns falsely after having healed — a behavior change relative to round 6 introduced by this round's fix, i.e. a regression in the heal's coverage rather than in the previously closed properties.

Termination is now guaranteed and the cap is demonstrably load-bearing: with a writer that re-arms a stale true on every notification the real candidate returns from the synchronous stack in 1ms after exactly 8 passes and 8 extra writes, whereas a mutant of the same source with MAX_HEAL_PASSES=Infinity reached 201 passes and was stopped only by my harness's own gate — so the cap, not the argument, is what prevents the UI freeze. The cap does not throw (break, not throw), it does not clear any job state, and it does not lose an already-valid heal. The failure path that is NOT correct is the exit position: checking the cap before the zero-candidate rescan means pass 9 is never run even when it is known to be needed, so a bounded writer with exactly 9..N re-arms leaves the marker true (my probe: real passes=8 marker true vs mutant passes=10 marker false; N=12: 8/true vs 13/false), and the 7-re-arm case heals but still emits a console.warn whose text asserts an unhealed candidate that does not exist. F-3's termination argument verified by instrumentation rather than by reading: the normal path genuinely does not break at `if (!healPending) break` (measured 0 hits), it exits at the zero-candidate rescan (1 hit), with passes=1, predicate calls=1, self-inflicted identity change=1, re-entry 1 and healPending set 1 — every figure the comment asserts. Other failure paths re-checked: a rejected click has no side effects and does give visible feedback; a marker legitimized by a queued job on another canvas is never mis-cleared; abort/cancel paths leave no permanent lock.

Most round-7 prose repairs are accurate and were verified against the code rather than trusted. F-2: the (marker|status) enumeration is now explicitly non-exhaustive and `true|idle` is genuinely produced by useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:138-142 (`queued: true, status: "idle"`), so adding it is correct and the one-directional invariant is preserved. F-3: the note that the normal path does NOT exit at `if (!healPending) break` is true by instrumentation (0 hits there) and the real exit is the zero-candidate rescan (1 hit). F-4: exactly 3 `queued:false` write sites exist in imageGenerationExecution.ts (:213, :227, :267) and the comment's line references match. The self-catch that `import.meta.hot` appears only in that comment itself is confirmed (1 occurrence repo-wide). The cap's own doc comment correctly distinguishes a per-synchronous-stack pass cap from a 'total heals' cap and correctly describes when a second pass is needed. Fails maintainability: (a) the dependency figure '21 in-repo + 7 bare externals' at :824 does not match the real graph, which gives 22 + 7 under every method tried (and 20 or 45 under others), so the number is unsubstantiated in a comment that presents it as measured — the fourth consecutive round in which a prose figure in this file is wrong; (b) the deferral-loop comment at :854-860 describes the cap's cost as 'may miss one heal' without noting that the cost is paid a full pass early and can be paid even when the remaining candidate would have been cleared, and the console.warn text at :943-944 asserts '仍有陈旧 queued 标记未复核' in a case where nothing remains to re-examine, which will mislead whoever debugs the next report of that warning.

Costs measured, not asserted. The cap bounds the worst case tightly: the pathological synchronous stack completed in 1ms for 8 passes (mutant: 201 passes in 6ms before my gate stopped it), so the user-visible freeze this cap exists to prevent is genuinely prevented and the cap's own overhead is negligible. The normal path is unchanged from round 6 and stays at its minimum: 1 pass, 1 predicate call, 1 self-inflicted identity change, with no extra writes — confirmed by instrumenting passes and the predicate rather than by reading the comment. The zero-candidate early return still precedes the reentrancy flag and every write, so a node whose marker is already correct produces no identity change, no subscriber hit and no canvas write, i.e. no extra 800ms-debounced persistence churn (probe-r3-finally-churn: 0 subscribe hits). The cap does not add any allocation, timer or async hop; it is a single integer compare. The only performance-adjacent caveat is semantic rather than cost-related and is recorded under failure_paths: exiting before the zero-candidate rescan forgoes a pass that may have been needed, which trades correctness margin for one fewer scan.
